## What We Did

<!-- CHANGE THIS: replace with your own notes -->

This week, I set up the basic workflow for my course portfolio. I created a
repository from the course template, cloned it to my computer with GitHub
Desktop, opened the project in RStudio, edited a Quarto file, and rendered it
as a webpage. I then committed and pushed the changes to GitHub so that they
could appear on my GitHub Pages site.

I also learned that a website can be understood as a collection of HTML files
stored on a computer or server. Quarto helps create those HTML files: I write
content in a `.qmd` file, and Quarto renders it into an `.html` file that a web
browser can display.



## Key Concepts

Three places a file can live:

1. **My computer** — where I edit
2. **GitHub.com** — where it's stored
3. **My live site** — what the world sees

The loop: **Edit → Save → Render → Commit → Push → wait → refresh**

## Proving R Works

The chunk below runs when this page renders. If you can see a result underneath
it on your published site, R and Quarto are talking to each other correctly.

```{r}
sessionInfo()$R.version$version.string
```
